headword: {満員電車|まんいんでんしゃ}

definitions.gloss: packed train; crowded train; train at full capacity
definitions.explanation: a train that is extremely crowded with passengers, typically during rush hours in urban Japan

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{満員電車|まんいんでんしゃ}で{通勤|つうきん}している。
examples.english: I commute on a packed train every morning.

examples.japanese: {満員電車|まんいんでんしゃ}に{乗|の}るのはストレスがたまる。
{満員電車|まんいんでんしゃ}を{避|さ}けるために、{早|はや}めに{家|いえ}を{出|で}るようにしている。
examples.english: I try to leave home early to avoid the packed trains.

notes:
FORMATION:
{満員|まんいん} (full capacity) + {電車|でんしゃ} (train) → full-capacity train

JAPANESE RUSH HOUR:
During peak commuting hours ({通勤|つうきん}ラッシュ) in major cities like Tokyo and Osaka, trains can reach 180-200% of their designed capacity.

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {通勤|つうきん}ラッシュ (commuter rush)
- {帰宅|きたく}ラッシュ (evening rush)
- {吊|つ}り{革|かわ} (hanging strap)
- {押|お}し{屋|や} (train pusher - staff who push passengers into trains)

COMMON EXPERIENCES:
- {身動|みうご}きが{取|と}れない (unable to move)
- {潰|つぶ}されそう (feeling crushed)
- スマホも{見|み}られない (can't even look at phone)

TIPS FOR AVOIDING:
- {時差出勤|じさしゅっきん} (staggered commuting)
- リモートワーク (remote work)
- {各駅停車|かくえきていしゃ}に{乗|の}る (take the local train)
